newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes hostage talks in Peru.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes hostage talks in Peru.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday that talks between Peru's government and Marxist guerrillas showed a peaceful solution was possible to the Lima hostage crisis, but Washington still believed no concessions should be made to "terrorists".

Peruvian government negotiator Domingo Palermo held what were called "preliminary conversations" on Tuesday with Rolly Rojas, a spokesman for Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who have been holding 72 hostages for 57 days.
"We view this as a positive step forward because we think there's a premium on getting to a peaceful solution of this problem," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"We think that these kinds of meetings are necessary to build momentum for a peaceful solution."

"The fact that they, after so many weeks, have arrived at the point where they can talk to each other directly in a rational way is a strong indicator that a peaceful solution is possible, and we are encouraging that," Burns added.
But, he added: "The United States does not believe that terrorists should succeed and we do not believe that concessions should be made to them."
Burns said Washington was heartened that Peruvian President Albert Fujimori had agreed on this last point during a visit to Washington last week.
U.S. officials have declined comment on specific solutions that might be reached to the crisis, saying they do not want to "micromanage" it.
The guerrillas, who seized their hostages at a reception at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, have demanded the release of some 400 jailed comrades.
